Their reunion at Wilmington International Airport showcased multiple surprises: Misty's weight loss, their three-year-old daughter Nevhah's growth, and a new family home purchased during Larry's absence. Misty maintained secrecy by avoiding full-body photos online. 'I kept pictures off Facebook and only sent shoulder-up images,' she told WSFA. Larry initially didn't recognize his transformed wife at the airport until their emotional embrace. 'This is incredible,' Larry stated. 'I've always loved her, but she achieved her personal goal.' He also marveled at their daughter's development and expressed appreciation for the new house. The family anticipates stable time together before any future deployments.

article_content: (CNN) -- Cambodia's Khmer Rouge regime (1975-1979) caused nearly 1.7 million deaths - approximately a quarter of the population - through executions, forced labor, starvation, and disease. A UN-backed tribunal has convicted three former leaders of crimes against humanity in landmark cases. Nuon Chea ('Brother Number Two') and Khieu Samphan (former president of Democratic Kampuchea) received life sentences in 2014. Kaing Guek Eav ('Comrade Duch'), who oversaw the S-21 prison where 14,000 died, was convicted in 2010 with his sentence finalized to life imprisonment in 2012. Key historical developments: 1970: Coup installs Lon Nol regime, Prince Sihanouk allies with Khmer Rouge Apr 1975: Khmer Rouge captures Phnom Penh, forces 2 million into rural labor Jan 1979: Vietnamese forces end Khmer Rouge rule, begin occupation Oct 1991: Paris Peace Accords establish UN transitional authority 2003: UN-Cambodia agreement creates hybrid tribunal 2010-2014: Convictions of Duch, Nuon Chea, and Khieu Samphan Sources: Cambodia Tribunal Monitor, Extraordinary Chambers in the Courts of Cambodia, UN records

article_content: A federal jury determined Friday that Naeem Williams qualifies for the death penalty in Hawaii's first federal capital case since statehood. The panel found the former soldier met all legal requirements for capital punishment in the 2005 murder of his 5-year-old daughter Talia through sustained abuse. Sentencing deliberations between death or life imprisonment without parole begin Wednesday. The case highlights jurisdictional complexities: Hawaii abolished capital punishment in 1957, but federal law applies as the crime occurred on military property. Last month's conviction detailed systematic torture including daily belt beatings, food deprivation, and violent restraints that led to Talia's fatal injuries. Defense arguments focused on Williams' cognitive limitations, while prosecutors emphasized the victim's vulnerability. Trial testimony revealed Talia sustained chest injuries with visible knuckle imprints from her father's final assault, prompting her removal from school to hide abuse evidence. Stepdaughter Delilah Williams, testifying under a plea deal for a 20-year sentence, described extreme abuse methods including duct-tape restraints and traumatic hair removal. U.S. District Judge Seabright ordered her sentencing to await conclusion of Naeem Williams' trial proceedings.

article_content: KABUL, Afghanistan (CNN) – Hashmat Khalil Karzai, a cousin of Afghan President Hamid Karzai and prominent political figure in Kandahar province, was killed in a suicide bombing during Eid al-Fitr celebrations, officials confirmed Tuesday. The attack occurred when a bomber detonated explosives at Karzai's residence while he was meeting visitors. Hashmat Karzai served on Kandahar's provincial council and supported presidential candidate Dr. Ashraf Ghani Ahmadzai. This marks the third assassination of a Karzai family member in 15 years, following the 2011 killing of the president's half-brother Ahmed Wali Karzai (then Kandahar provincial council chief) and the 1999 death of his father Abdul Ahad Karzai. The Taliban claimed responsibility for previous attacks on the family. President Karzai, preparing to leave office after disputed elections, stated: 'Afghans face daily terrorism – my family is not exempt from this tragedy.'

Der Anschlag ereignete sich, als ein Attentäter in Karzais Wohnhaus Sprengstoff detonierte, während dieser Gäste empfing. Hashmat Karzai war Mitglied des Kandahar-Provinzrats und unterstützte Präsidentschaftskandidat Dr. Ashraf Ghani Ahmadzai. article_content: While memes dominate today's social media landscape, their roots stretch back to the early days of digital connectivity. Long before viral trends became an industry, pioneering online communities developed cultural touchstones through creative expression. Let's explore 10 foundational memes that shaped internet culture: Leetspeak (1980s): Emerging from hacker circles, this alphanumeric code language popularized terms like 'n00bs' and 'pwned,' influencing gaming vernacular for decades. Godwin's Law (1990): This Usenet-era principle humorously notes how online debates inevitably reference Nazis, creating an enduring rule for forum etiquette. Hamster Dance (1998): This pixelated animation sparked early viral sharing through email chains, predating modern video memes. 'All Your Base' (1998): A mistranslation from Japanese game Zero Wing inspired mass remixing, highlighting humor in localization errors. YTMND (2001): This platform transformed a Sean Connery movie quote into a creative hub for audio-visual mashups. Anonymous (2003): Originating as 4chan pranksters before evolving into hacktivism post-2008 Chanology project. FAIL Culture (2000s): Capitalizing on schadenfreude, this trend spawned enduring reaction symbols like facepalms. Badger Loop (2003): Jonti Picking's hypnotic animation showcased repetitive humor's viral potential. LOLcats (2007): Feline photos with quirky captions standardized meme formats using Impact font. Rickrolling (2007): This bait-and-switch prank revived Rick Astley's '80s hit while popularizing trolling culture.

article_content: Melbourne photographer Jonas Peterson has photographed weddings worldwide, but his recent assignment in Kenya's Masai Mara surpassed even his most idyllic locations. The Swedish-Australian photographer, with over 300 global weddings documented, found himself profoundly moved by the African savanna's raw beauty during Nina and Sebastian's September wedding. 'Some places stay with you forever,' Peterson reflected. 'When the couple requested Masai Mara, I never anticipated how deeply this land would resonate. It awakened creative dimensions I didn't know existed.' The ceremony coincided with the annual wildebeest migration from Tanzania's Serengeti National Park to Kenya's Masai Mara, creating a living backdrop of wildlife. 'We required guards to prevent lion intrusions,' Peterson noted. 'It resembled the Garden of Eden - endless plains teeming with millions of animals.' Nina, a wildlife photographer, had formed strong bonds with Maasai communities through her lion conservation project. This connection inspired the couple to incorporate traditional elements: an arch symbolizing Maasai home entrances, enkarewa jewelry gifted by local friends, and warriors participating in celebrations. 'Our cultures and nature merged perfectly,' Nina stated. Despite storm clouds gathering, the weather held during vows. Peterson admitted struggling to focus: 'The savannah's grandeur kept overwhelming my senses. Location matters less than authentic emotion, but here we had both.' The couple's two-year-old daughter and Maasai community members shared in what Peterson declared his most memorable professional experience: 'A perfect convergence of culture, emotion, and environment.'

article_content: Authorities in southern Japan are searching for Craig Arnold, an acclaimed American poet and University of Wyoming professor who disappeared during a volcanic research trip. The 41-year-old academic failed to return from a solo hike on Kuchinoerabujima Island on Monday while gathering material for a book about volcanoes. A 60-person team with helicopters and canine units has located footprints confirming Arnold began the ascent but found no further traces. The U.S. Air Force deployed four Okinawa-based helicopters on Thursday at the embassy's request to assist Japanese authorities in the ongoing operation, which will continue through Sunday. Arnold, a two-time poetry award winner and recipient of prestigious fellowships, typically uses guides for dangerous climbs but undertook this expedition alone. Colleagues describe him as drawn to extreme environments that inspire his award-winning work.

Ein 60-köpfiges Rettungsteam mit Hubschraubern und Spürhunden entdeckte Fußspuren, die seinen Aufstieg belegen. Die US-Luftwaffe unterstützte die Suche am Donnerstag mit vier Hubschraubern von ihrer Basis in Okinawa auf Ersuchen der Botschaft. Die Suchaktion läuft bis Sonntag. article_content: The Grunenthal Group, creator of the birth defect-causing drug thalidomide (marketed as Contergan in Germany), issued its first formal apology in 50 years to victims worldwide. CEO Harald Stock expressed regret during the September 2012 unveiling of a memorial statue in Stolberg, acknowledging the company's prolonged silence and the suffering endured by families. UK advocates like Freddie Astbury, born without limbs in 1959, criticized the gesture as inadequate, noting Diageo's 2005 compensation increase to £6.5 million annually. Over 10,000 children were born with severe disabilities before thalidomide's 1961 withdrawal. Ongoing legal battles include Australian court cases and a planned class action representing 100 victims.

Vorstand Harald Stock drückte bei der Enthüllung einer Gedenkstatue im September 2012 in Stolberg Reue aus und gestand das jahrzehntelange Schweigen des Unternehmens ein. Britische Betroffenenvertreter wie Freddie Astbury, der 1959 ohne Arme und Beine zur Welt kam, bewerteten die Entschuldigung als ungenügend und verwiesen auf die 2005 von Diageo erhöhten Entschädigungszahlungen von jährlich 6,5 Millionen Pfund. article_content: A security guard died from a self-inflicted gunshot wound at the Swedish prime minister's official residence on Friday afternoon. Prime Minister Fredrik Reinfeldt was not present during the incident, and his son, who was in the building, remained unharmed. Swedish newspaper Aftonbladet reported the death, which police spokesperson Towe Hagg confirmed: 'A deceased male was found inside Sagerska Palace. While no criminal activity is suspected, investigators are gathering evidence.' The prime minister's spokesperson Markus Friberg confirmed Reinfeldt was visiting Aftonbladet's offices during the incident. Stockholm police emphasized the guard worked for private security firm Svensk Bevakningstjänst, not the PM's personal protection team. The Sagerska Palace, located along Stockholm's waterfront, employs both private guards and state security personnel. Security Service spokeswoman Sirpa Franzen confirmed no government personnel were affected, stating: 'There's currently no connection to parliamentary or government operations.' Sweden strengthened political security following the 1986 assassination of PM Olof Palme and the 2003 killing of Foreign Minister Anna Lindh. The country maintains relatively open access to government buildings despite these measures.

Polizeisprecherin Towe Hagg bestätigte: 'Im Sagerska Palast wurde ein verstorbener Mann aufgefunden. Obwohl wir kein Verbrechen vermuten, werden derzeit Beweise gesichert.' Regierungssprecher Markus Friberg teilte mit, Reinfeldt habe zum Zeitpunkt des Geschehens die Redaktion der Aftonbladet besucht. Die Stockholmer Polizei betonte, der Wachmann sei bei der privaten Sicherheitsfirma Svensk Bevakningstjänst angestellt gewesen – nicht im persönlichen Schutzteam des Premierministers. Schweden verschärfte den Schutz für Politiker nach der Ermordung von Premierminister Olof Palme 1986 und der Tötung von Außenministerin Anna Lindh 2003. Trotz dieser Maßnahmen bleibt der Zugang zu Regierungsgebäuden vergleichsweise offen.

article_content: Seattle residents have until December 3 to experience 'Renegade Edo and Paris' - an exhibition contrasting 18th-century Japanese ukiyo-e woodcuts with 19th-century French Art Nouveau posters at the Seattle Asian Art Museum. Situated in Volunteer Park (not to be confused with the downtown location featuring new Calder works), this display explores cultural connections between Edo-era Tokyo and fin-de-siècle Paris. The exhibition demonstrates how both cities' social transformations, fueled by growing middle classes, sparked artistic innovation in theater and visual arts. Visitors can examine delicate Japanese prints alongside monumental Toulouse-Lautrec posters - familiar in books but breathtaking at original scale. The museum building itself holds cinematic history, having portrayed Hilly Blue's mansion in the 1985 film 'Trouble In Mind' starring drag icon Divine.

Kuratorisch wird aufgezeigt, wie gesellschaftliche Umbrüche durch aufstrebende Mittelschichten in beiden Städten künstlerische Innovationen im Theater- und Kunstbereich antrieben. Besucher können filigrane Holzdrucke bewundern, die neben großformatigen Toulouse-Lautrec-Lithografien präsentiert werden - in Originalgröße noch imposanter als in Abbildungen. article_content: A Flagstaff police officer with less than a year of service was fatally wounded Saturday while responding to a domestic violence call. Tyler Stewart, 24, sustained a gunshot wound to the face during an altercation with suspect Robert W. Smith around 1:30 PM. Authorities report Smith fired multiple rounds at Stewart before taking his own life. Colleagues rushed to the 800 block of West Clay Avenue after Stewart activated his emergency alert system but couldn't establish radio contact. article_content: LONDON, England (CNN) – Alternative treatments vary widely across global regions. While some Western medical practitioners remain skeptical, these methods remain integral to healthcare systems worldwide. In Japan, shark cartilage is consumed for perceived health benefits, while 80% of populations in parts of Asia and Africa rely on traditional medicine as primary care. Shark fin has been used in Asian traditional medicine for centuries, often promoted as promoting wellness and claimed to have anti-cancer properties. Sold as powder, tablets, or whole fins, its Western popularity grew after the 1992 book 'Sharks Don't Get Cancer.' However, scientific evidence contradicts these claims: A 2000 George Washington University Medical Center study documented over 40 tumors in sharks, skates, and rays. Clinical trials like a 1998 study by the Independent Cancer Treatment Research Foundation found no anti-cancer benefits. Cancer Research UK states there's no evidence supporting shark cartilage treatments. Environmentalists criticize shark fin harvesting through 'finning' – removing fins from live sharks and discarding the bodies at sea. This practice threatens shark populations. In South Africa's Faraday market, 'muti' practitioners use herbs and animal parts for treatments. 'Sangomas' diagnose illnesses through spiritual communication, referring patients to 'inyangas' who prepare remedies for physical and psychological conditions. Acupuncture, a 2,000-year-old Chinese practice, balances 'qi' energy flow through meridians. Modern practitioners like the British Acupuncture Council's Marian Rose combine traditional pulse diagnosis with questions about health history. Research, including work by Dr Mike Cummings of the British Medical Acupuncture Association, shows acupuncture effectively treats pain by stimulating nerves and modulating sensory input. While some traditional treatments lack scientific backing, others like acupuncture gain recognition through research, potentially complementing modern medicine.

Haifischflossen werden seit Jahrhunderten in der asiatischen Traditionellen Medizin verwendet – oft als Stärkungsmittel mit angeblichen Anti-Krebs-Eigenschaften beworben. Als Pulver, Tabletten oder ganze Flossen verkauft, gewannen sie im Westen nach Erscheinen des Buches 'Haie bekommen keinen Krebs' (1992) an Popularität. article_content: Over a year after Ethiopia's November 2022 peace agreement, many Tigrayans remain displaced as areas of their region stay occupied by federal government-allied forces. While the deal between national authorities and the Tigray People's Liberation Front stopped active fighting, civilians like Wekeynos Guesh continue facing obstacles to returning home. The conflict erupted in November 2020 when Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed deployed federal troops alongside Amhara regional forces and Eritrean soldiers. United Nations data shows 1.8 million people were displaced, while former Nigerian President Olusegun Obasanjo - the African Union's chief mediator - estimates 600,000 conflict-related deaths. Though banking services have resumed and some civil servant salaries restored, reconstruction lags. The Irob ethnic minority, numbering approximately 60,000, warns of cultural extinction due to prolonged displacement. Muruts Hagos from Alitena reports Eritrean forces looted his hometown, forcing residents into overcrowded Mekelle camps where food aid suspensions worsen conditions. Humanitarian workers describe strained resources, with IDPs competing for aid amid Ethiopia's Amhara conflict and Sudan's crisis. Some displaced people resort to petty crime as shelters overflow and schools reopen, displacing camp residents again. Experts identify multiple peace process flaws: Oslo University's Kjetil Tronvoll highlights absent timelines for troop withdrawals and unaddressed sexual violence. Amnesty International's Suad Nur criticizes justice discussions favoring reconciliation over accountability, leaving survivors without recourse. With federal forces engaged in new conflicts elsewhere, displaced Tigrayans question ongoing security justifications. As former fighter Wekeynos notes: 'We've disarmed... If federal police control western Tigray now, what prevents our return?'

Zwar stoppte die Vereinbarung zwischen Addis Abeba und der Tigray-Volksbefreiungsfront (TPLF) die Kampfhandlungen, doch Zivilisten wie Wekeynos Guesh berichten weiterhin von unüberwindbaren Rückkehrhindernissen. Der Konflikt eskalierte im November 2020, als Premierminister Abiy Ahmed äthiopische Streitkräfte zusammen mit verbündeten Amhara-Milizen und eritreischen Soldaten in die Region entsandte. Laut UN-Angaben wurden 1,8 Millionen Menschen vertrieben, während der ehemalige nigerianische Präsident Olusegun Obasanjo – als Vermittler der Afrikanischen Union – von etwa 600.000 kriegsbedingten Todesopfern ausgeht. Obwohl Bankdienstleistungen wiederaufgenommen wurden und einige Gehälter staatlicher Angestellter nachgezahlt werden, kommt der Wiederaufbau nur langsam voran. Die rund 60.000 Angehörigen der Irob-Minderheit warnen vor dem Aussterben ihrer Kultur durch anhaltende Vertreibung. Muruts Hagos aus Alitena schildert, wie eritreische Truppen seine Heimatstadt plünderten und Bewohner in überfüllte Lager in Mekelle zwangen, wo ausgesetzte Lebensmittelhilfen des Welternährungsprogramms (WFP) die Situation verschlimmern. Humanitarbeiter berichten von extrem knappen Ressourcen, da Binnenvertriebene gleichzeitig mit den Folgen des Amhara-Konflikts in Äthiopien und der Krise im Sudan um Hilfe konkurrieren. Einige Vertriebene greifen zu Diebstählen, da wiedereröffnete Schulen Lagerbewohner erneut obdachlos machen und Unterkünfte überfüllt sind. Experten benennen mehrere Schwachstellen im Friedensprozess: Kjetil Tronvoll von der Universität Oslo kritisiert fehlende Zeitpläne für Truppenabzüge und nicht aufgearbeitete sexualisierte Gewalt. Suad Nur von Amnesty International verurteilt Justizdebatten, die politische Versöhnung über die Rechte von Opfern stellen. Während äthiopische Sicherheitskräfte in anderen Landesteilen neue Konflikte austragen, stellen Vertriebene die anhaltenden Sicherheitsbegründungen infrage. Wie der ehemalige Kämpfer Wekeynos betont: 'Wir haben die Waffen abgegeben... Wenn jetzt Bundespolizei Westtigray kontrolliert, was verhindert dann unsere Rückkehr?'

article_content: With her eyes closed and face adorned with white paint, sequins, and paper flowers, Bulgarian bride Fatme Inus upheld Ribnovo's centuries-old 'gelena' tradition during her winter wedding. The remote mountain town maintains strict customs including alcohol-free receptions and pre-marital chastity. Brides accumulate handmade dowries displayed on 50-meter-long wooden scaffolds, while the community participates in traditional horo dances. Ethnographers note the ritual's uncertain origins, with Margarita Karamihova from the Bulgarian Academy of Science suggesting it's an 'invented tradition' reinforcing Pomak identity. Mayor Ahmed Bashev details historical suppression of Pomak weddings under Communist rule. Despite economic pressures driving male migration, Ribnovo's 3,500 residents preserve cultural continuity through elaborate rituals, supported by two mosques and ten clerics.

article_content: (CNN) Studio 54 remains emblematic of 1970s glamour. Few retain clear memories of the legendary New York nightclub, but photographer Tod Papageorge preserves its legacy through rediscovered images now published in 'Studio 54.' The first edition sold out; a 'silver edition' releases December 23. 'My Studio 54 involvement was serendipitous,' Papageorge told CNN. 'My then-girlfriend had access. When offered photography access, I seized the opportunity.' Opened in 1977 by Steve Rubell and Ian Schrager, the converted theater became Manhattan's epicenter of celebrity culture. A liquor license raid one month post-opening enhanced its rebellious allure. Regulars included Elizabeth Taylor, Andy Warhol, and Salvador Dali. 'The energy was electric,' Papageorge recalled. 'People recognized this fleeting magic. Dancers moved wildly, celebrities retreated to private rooms, and the atmosphere crackled with excitement.' Memorable events included a New Year's Eve party with four tons of glitter creating a 'stardust' effect and fashion gift boxes dropped from nets. The club's strict door policy enforced by Mark Benecke curated a mix of elites through opaque selection criteria. The club closed in 1981 amid owner tax evasion charges. Papageorge connects this period to emerging AIDS reports: 'Many photographed later died from it. This marked the end of an unbridled era.' Rediscovering his archive after 35 years, Papageorge states: 'These images hold up powerfully. They capture a pivotal cultural moment before tragedy reshaped our world.'

Die Erstauflage ist vergriffen; eine 'Silber-Edition' erscheint am 23. Dezember. 'Meine Verbindung zu Studio 54 war ein Zufall,' verriet Papageorge CNN. 'Meine damalige Freundin hatte Zugang. article_content: (CNN) -- There's likely no turning back this time. Jay Leno concludes his 22-year tenure as host of 'The Tonight Show' on Thursday. Jimmy Fallon, after less than five years hosting NBC's 'Late Night,' assumes the role on February 17, 2014. His replacement, 'Saturday Night Live' veteran Seth Meyers, will take over 'Late Night' a week later. NBC hasn't fully explained why it's replacing Leno, who dominates late-night ratings across key demographics, including the advertiser-coveted 18-49 age group. He outperforms Fallon, David Letterman, Jimmy Kimmel, and others. The network's sole justification in its April 2013 announcement stated: 'Jimmy Fallon is a unique talent and this is his time.' Leno leaves a complex legacy beyond NBC's controversial handling of his career. His departure may reshape late-night TV dynamics. While critics often dismissed him as unrefined, history may remember Leno as the 'people's champion' due to his consistent ratings success. Leno's monologue prowess rivaled Johnny Carson's, delivering reliable humor through segments like 'Headlines' and 'Jaywalking.' However, interview segments often felt scripted compared to Carson's spontaneous style. At 63, Leno exits as NBC develops new projects for 76-year-old Bill Cosby - an ironic contrast. Fallon brings youthful energy and social media savvy (11.4M Twitter followers) but must strengthen his monologue skills. Meanwhile, Letterman faces new competition from a New York-based peer for the first time in his CBS career. Kimmel could benefit from West Coast exclusivity against East Coast rivals. The succession plan raises questions: At 40, Meyers is older than Fallon, breaking NBC's tradition of grooming younger hosts. His future prospects remain uncertain in the evolving late-night landscape.

article_content: MOSCOW (CNN) – Four bodies have been recovered and 49 people remain missing after an offshore drilling rig capsized in Russia's Sea of Okhotsk, according to the Emergency Situations Ministry. Fourteen crew members were rescued from the Kolskaya platform, which was being towed from Kamchatka when pumps failed during relocation. Rescue operations continue despite storm conditions, with authorities noting the four individuals found without vital signs require formal recovery before death confirmation. The Gazprom-contracted rig carried 67 personnel. The Magadan icebreaker and Naftogaz-55 tugboat continue nighttime search efforts 200 km from Sakhalin Island, where the rig operated at 3,500 meters depth. Helicopters will resume operations at dawn. Regional emergencies spokesperson Taimuraz Kasayev confirmed no environmental threat exists due to hermetically sealed fuel tanks. Russia Today reported the sinking resulted from pump failure during towing operations.

article_content: Police in Washington state are searching for two-year-old Sky Metalwala, who disappeared after his mother left him unattended in an unlocked car on November 6, 2011. Court records reveal that Julia Biryukova and Solomon Metalwala, the child's parents, had previously faced charges of reckless endangerment in 2009 for leaving another child alone in a vehicle. The case was dismissed in early 2011 after they completed probation, 40 hours of community service, and parenting classes. Biryukova, who separated from her husband in 2010, told authorities she left Sky buckled in her silver Acura while walking with her four-year-old daughter to a gas station approximately one mile away. Upon returning an hour later, the boy was missing. Police searched a 20-block area without success. Biryukova had obtained a restraining order against Solomon in 2010, alleging physical abuse and threats, including an incident where he allegedly assaulted her for letting Sky sleep too long as an infant. The father's legal representative declined to comment. Authorities have not determined whether Sky wandered off or was abducted.

article_content: Google has joined forces with the FBI to warn over 500,000 users about the persistent DNSChanger malware affecting 350,000+ devices globally. Computers infected with this Estonian-origin threat face internet disconnection on July 9 when emergency servers sunset. The malware secretly reroutes users to illegal sites while preventing security updates. Although FBI-established temporary servers initially maintained access, they'll be retired for cost efficiency. Google's multilingual alerts target affected users through search results, with 85,000 U.S. and 20,000 U.K. devices still compromised. The DNSChanger Working Group collaborates to find solutions before the March 8 court deadline, aiming to prevent widespread internet outages when surrogate servers potentially go offline.

article_content: Actor Robin Williams was cremated with his ashes scattered in San Francisco Bay on August 12, 2014, according to official documents obtained by CNN. The Marin County Coroner's Office continues to investigate the August 11 death initially attributed to suicide by hanging using a belt. Assistant Deputy Chief Coroner Lt. Keith Boyd confirmed Williams had been receiving treatment for depression prior to his death, including a July 2014 stay at a treatment facility. While declining to comment on the existence of a suicide note, Boyd noted the ongoing nature of the investigation. Williams' widow Susan Schneider clarified her husband had maintained sobriety while managing depression, anxiety, and early-stage Parkinson's disease. 'Robin dedicated his life to bringing joy through his work and charitable efforts,' Schneider stated, addressing previous media speculation about substance use.

By Steve Robson | Published: 07:59 EST, 8 January 2013 | Updated: 10:38 EST, 8 January 2013

Susan Hatton faces a legal challenge after receiving a £167 fine for stopping in a bus lane for seven seconds to assist her elderly father. The 61-year-old pulled over at a bus stop on Eastwood Road North in Leigh, Essex, to help her 84-year-old father Ken exit the vehicle. Southend Council's surveillance vehicle recorded the incident and issued an initial £35 penalty, which later increased to £167.

Ms. Hatton, who is contesting the fine, stated: 'My father had emphysema in both lungs and couldn't walk far. Six weeks after this incident, he was hospitalized with pneumonia. At the time, I didn't see the need for a blue badge as he only traveled short distances. I remained in the vehicle during the brief stop.'

The council provided timestamped images showing the stop duration from 11:21:38 to 11:21:45. Despite Ms. Hatton's appeals, the council upheld the fine and involved bailiffs for collection.

Derek Kenyon, Southend Council's parking manager, confirmed the challenge was rejected but noted: 'We've provided clear guidance on further appeal steps should the resident wish to pursue this matter.'

article_content: Shellie Zimmerman, wife of George Zimmerman, was taken into custody Tuesday on allegations of providing false financial information during her husband's bond proceedings. Authorities claim the 25-year-old misrepresented their monetary resources during an April 20 hearing for George Zimmerman's second-degree murder case involving Trayvon Martin's death. Court documents reveal substantial fund movements between family accounts around the time of the bond hearing. Prosecutors allege $47,000 moved to George's sister's account and over $74,000 transferred to Shellie's personal account in April. Following George's release after posting 10% of his $150,000 bond, $85,500 reportedly flowed back to his account. State Attorney Angela Corey contends the couple used coded language to conceal funds from the court. Defense attorneys counter that $204,000 raised through online donations remains mostly in an independently managed trust, with $150,000 allocated for legal defense and $30,000 spent on relocation costs. The defense acknowledges disclosure delays, attributing them to confusion and fear. They maintain proper fund management since discovery, with remaining funds covering living expenses during trial. Shellie Zimmerman faces formal charges July 31.

article_content: Rickie Fowler secured his maiden PGA Tour victory at the 2012 Wells Fargo Championship, defeating world number one Rory McIlroy and D.A. Points in a playoff showdown. The breakthrough occurred at Quail Hollow - the same venue where McIlroy had claimed his breakthrough U.S. win two years earlier with a historic final round. Clad in his trademark orange outfit and sporting a throwback mustache, Fowler delivered a clutch wedge shot on the notoriously difficult 18th hole. This decisive moment, achieved on a hole that yielded only four birdies all day, earned him $1.17 million and propelled him to 15th in FedEx Cup standings and 24th in world rankings. McIlroy, who regained the top ranking with his second-place finish, praised Fowler's composure: 'He's endured significant scrutiny pursuing that first victory. This should alleviate that pressure.' Fowler humorously contrasted his single win with Phil Mickelson's 40, vowing to build on this success. The victory enhances Fowler's chances for Ryder Cup selection as Team USA prepares for Medinah. Across the Atlantic, Francesco Molinari strengthened his European Ryder Cup bid by winning the Spanish Open, climbing to 10th in European team standings.

article_content: UK supermarket Morrisons faced criticism after projecting a giant baguette advertisement onto the Angel of North sculpture in Gateshead. The controversial marketing move, intended to promote price reductions amid competition with discount chains Lidl and Aldi, drew swift backlash for using the iconic artwork without authorization. A 175-foot image of French bread bearing the slogan 'I'm cheaper' illuminated the steel statue, prompting accusations of cultural insensitivity. Sculptor Antony Gormley, creator of the 208-tonne landmark installed in 1998, publicly objected to the unauthorized commercial use. Gateshead Council confirmed the projection violated established protocols for artwork engagement. Social media erupted with outrage, with users condemning the act as 'philistine' and threatening boycotts. Morrisons later apologized, stating: 'We regret any offense caused by our attempt at lighthearted promotion. While aiming to bring joy, we recognize this approach missed the mark. Our deep connection to northern communities makes this misjudgment particularly regrettable.' The Angel of North remains a symbol of industrial heritage, standing atop a former coal mine. Designed to honor mining history while looking toward Britain's future, its 175-foot wingspan – wider than a Boeing 757's – requires only septennial inspections due to structural stability.

Unsere tiefe Verbundenheit mit Nordengland macht diesen Fehltritt besonders schmerzlich.' Der Engel des Nordens bleibt ein Symbol industriellen Erbes und steht auf einem stillgelegten Kohlebergwerk. Mit 53 Metern Flügelspannweite – breiter als eine Boeing 757 – benötigt sie dank stabiler Konstruktion nur alle sieben Jahre Inspektionen.

article_content: Three decades after implementation, the National Organ Transplant Act's unintended consequences continue fueling a health crisis. While designed to prevent organ trafficking, its compensation restrictions now leave over 120,000 Americans on transplant waitlists - more citizens than perished in all U.S. wars since WWII combined. Financial barriers remain insurmountable for most potential donors. Though recipients may cover travel and lost wages, critical expenses like childcare, caregiver support, and business income losses go uncompensated. Census data shows merely 8% of households could manage the $5,000+ costs without hardship - a reality that prevented the author from donating to a dying friend despite medical approval. Current statistics reveal a dire situation: kidney patients constitute 100,000 waitlist entries, yet only 15% receive transplants. Over 400,000 Americans rely on dialysis, often deteriorating beyond transplant eligibility. Reform proposals advocate adopting proven disaster relief models, using prepaid debit systems to offset donor expenses without encouraging organ markets. While the 1984 law rightly prevented exploitative international donor schemes, its current form disproportionately impacts low-income citizens. article_content: Milford, Pennsylvania (CNN) – After 48 days of tension involving helicopters, armed officers, and constant speculation, northeastern Pennsylvania residents can finally breathe easier. Eric Matthew Frein, accused of killing a state trooper, was captured Thursday night by U.S. Marshals. Authorities transferred him to state police using the slain officer's handcuffs and vehicle in a symbolic gesture. 'We considered it appropriate,' stated State Police Commissioner Frank Noonan. Frein faces first-degree murder charges for the September 12 ambush at Blooming Grove barracks that killed Cpl. Bryon Dickson and injured Trooper Alex T. Douglass. The self-taught survivalist, known for anti-police sentiments, surrendered peacefully at an abandoned Tannersville airport during a routine sweep. A sniper rifle matching ballistic evidence was found nearby. At Friday's court hearing, Frein appeared with facial injuries but responded clearly to charges. Pike County District Attorney Raymond Tonkin announced plans to seek the death penalty. Governor Tom Corbett assured appropriate custody measures would be implemented. While Frein's precise motives remain unclear, authorities confirmed he made self-incriminating statements and maintained a diary. Computer evidence revealed years of planning, including research on evading manhunts. 'His goal was targeting law enforcement,' Noonan emphasized, noting concerns about potential further violence. The resolution brought community relief, with restored Halloween traditions and lifted hunting restrictions. The seven-week operation, costing approximately $10 million according to prosecutors, concluded with residents expressing gratitude through public celebrations and support for police efforts.

article_content: Approximately 300 homes and businesses near Arizona's Slide Rock State Park were evacuated Thursday as a 4,830-acre wildfire continued burning near the popular Sedona tourist destination. Authorities reported the fire remained 0% contained by late afternoon, with over 840 personnel including 15 specialized hotshot crews and three air tankers deployed to combat the blaze. The fire, originating Tuesday in the Oak Creek Canyon area four miles north of Sedona, has led to evacuation orders spanning a two- to three-mile radius from Slide Rock State Park to Sterling Springs Hatchery. Coconino County officials issued pre-evacuation notices to approximately 3,200 residents. 'As temperatures rise, we anticipate increased fire activity toward the northwest near Harding Point,' officials stated, warning of heavy smoke impacts in the Flagstaff region. The fire's cause remains under investigation, though authorities suspect human involvement. Local business owner Frank Garrison, who operates 20 rental cabins, described the personal toll: 'This is my home, livelihood, everything.' He joined a stream of evacuees Wednesday, having packed essential belongings. The Butterfly Garden Inn reported safely evacuating all guests and staff, posting on Facebook: 'We pray for our property's safety and the courageous firefighters battling this blaze.' Residents took extraordinary measures to protect properties, with Connor Packard spraying his mother-in-law's roof with a garden hose to ward against falling embers. 'Ash is already raining down,' he told local media. The challenging terrain of Oak Creek Canyon, combined with 30 mph winds, has complicated firefighting efforts. Slide Rock State Park—a historic 43-acre apple farm named among America's top 10 state parks by Fodor's Travel—remains closed as smoke from the fire reached Utah, 150 miles away. No injuries have been reported.

article_content: A 2010 ACLU report revealed Black Americans were arrested for marijuana possession at four times the rate of white Americans nationwide, despite comparable usage rates. Iowa showed the starkest disparity: Black residents faced 8.34 times more arrests than whites, despite comprising only 3% of the state's population. Similar patterns emerged in Washington D.C. (8.05x), Minnesota (7.81x), and Illinois (7.56x). Nationally, Black arrest rates rose from 537 to 716 per 100,000 people between 2001-2010, while white rates remained near 192 per 100,000. Experts attribute this to racial profiling and policing practices targeting 'open-air' drug markets in Black communities. The ACLU advocates for legalization or decriminalization to address systemic inequities, noting even affluent Black individuals face higher arrest risks than low-income whites.

(8,05x), Minnesota (7,81x) und Illinois (7,56x). The incident occurred amid heightened security awareness across Europe related to both the Israel-Hamas conflict and increasing drug-related violence in Brussels.

article_content: (CNN) — Flavia Wagner, a 35-year-old aid worker with Christian organization Samaritan's Purse, has been released after 105 days of captivity in Sudan's Darfur region, the group confirmed Monday. Wagner is 'exhausted but in good health,' according to their statement. The release coincides with reports of three Russian pilots working for a Sudanese aviation company being abducted in the same area. African Union-UN Mission spokesman Chris Cycmanick stated the pilots were taken Sunday in Nyala, South Darfur's capital. Cycmanick noted 12 abduction cases in Darfur this year, including Wagner's capture on May 18. Two Sudanese colleagues abducted with Wagner were released May 25. Samaritan's Purse, founded by evangelist Franklin Graham, reports providing $83.7 million in aid to Sudan since 2001, with 548 staff members currently operating in the country. The Darfur conflict, ongoing since 2003, involves government-linked Arab militias accused by UN agencies and human rights groups of targeting civilian tribes supporting rebels through systematic violence. The UN estimates 300,000 deaths and 2.5 million displaced persons, though Sudan disputes these figures. The International Criminal Court maintains an arrest warrant for Sudanese President Omar al-Bashir for alleged war crimes.

Demnach befindet sie sich 'in erschöpftem, aber stabilem Gesundheitszustand'. Die Freilassung erfolgte zeitgleich zur Entführung dreier russischer Piloten eines sudanesischen Luftfahrtunternehmens in derselben Region. Laut Chris Cycmanick, Sprecher der gemeinsamen Mission von Afrikanischer Union und UN, wurden die Pilote am Sonntag in Nyala, der Hauptstadt Süd-Darfurs, verschleppt. Cycmanick zufolge gab es 2023 bereits zwölf Entführungsfälle in Darfur, darunter Wagners Entführung am 18. Mai. Zwei mit ihr festgenommene sudanesische Kollegen waren bereits am 25. Mai freigekommen. Die von Evangelist Franklin Graham gegründete Organisation Samaritan's Purse gibt an, seit 2001 Hilfsleistungen im Wert von 83,7 Millionen US-Dollar im Sudan erbracht zu haben und derzeit mit 548 Mitarbeitern vor Ort aktiv zu sein. Der seit 2003 schwelende Darfur-Konflikt involviert regierungsnahe Milizen, denen die UNO und Menschenrechtsorganisationen systematische Gewalt gegen Zivilisten aus rebelliennahen Volksgruppen vorwerfen. Die Vereinten Nationen schätzen die Opferzahlen auf 300.000 Tote und 2,5 Millionen Vertriebene – Angaben, die der Sudan bestreitet. Der Internationale Strafgerichtshof hat ein Haftbefehl gegen Sudans Präsidenten Omar al-Baschir wegen mutmaßlicher Kriegsverbrechen ausgestellt.

article_content: Few people receive their own eulogies while alive. Jim Diers experienced this unusual situation firsthand. The Seattle resident began receiving condolence messages and life-status inquiries Thursday after Mayor Ed Murray's office erroneously announced his passing. 'I'm very saddened by the death of Jim Diers,' the mayor stated initially through CNN affiliate KIRO TV, praising Diers' 'immeasurable' community contributions. Officials later clarified they confused Diers with a similarly named deceased individual. Diers, meanwhile, posted on Facebook: 'I want to assure you I'm very much alive... I'm dead tired today, but otherwise feeling great! Thanks for concern, but I've no time for death.' The office retracted its statement within 30 minutes, confirming Diers' vitality to relieved loved ones.

Der Seattle-Einwohner erhielt am Donnerstag Kondolenznachrichten und Nachfragen zu seinem Gesundheitszustand, nachdem Bürgermeister Ed Murrays Büro fälschlicherweise seinen Tod meldete. 'Der Tod von Jim Diers macht mich zutiefst betroffen', hieß es zunächst in einer über den CNN-Partner KIRO TV verbreiteten Erklärung, in der Diers' 'unermessliche Verdienste' für die Gemeinschaft gewürdigt wurden. Später korrigierte sich die Behörde: Man habe Diers mit einem verstorbenen Namensvetter verwechselt. Diers selbst postete auf Facebook: 'Ich versichere, dass ich quicklebendig bin... Ich bin heute todmüde, aber ansonsten topfit! Danke für die Anteilnahme, aber für den Tod habe ich gerade echt keine Zeit.' Die Rücknahme der Fehlmeldung nach nur 30 Minuten brachte Erleichterung bei Angehörigen.

article_content: By Daily Mail Reporter | Updated: 11:06 EST, 27 February 2013 The story of a Nevada recluse's hidden gold reached a new chapter on Tuesday when part of the collection sold for over $3.5 million at auction. Bidders were drawn by both the mystery and the intrinsic value of the gold, which remained unknown until Walter Samaszko Jr.'s body was discovered in his Carson City home last year. The auction featured tight security with guards in bulletproof vests and helmets. Five bidders examined 11 lots of gold displayed in protective cases before competitive bidding commenced. Alan Rowe of Northern Nevada Coin secured nine lots, spending $617,000 personally and $2 million for Rare Coin Company of America Inc. 'We all have a hoarder instinct, but this degree is remarkable,' Rowe noted, emphasizing the story's value beyond mere metal worth. Remaining coins will be sold locally and nationally, with rarer pieces scheduled for a future auction. The full collection contained over 150 pounds of gold, including 2,900 Austrian coins (many from 1915), 5,000 Mexican pieces, and hundreds of British and U.S. coins dating to the 1880s. Meticulous records showed purchases dating to 1964 when gold was $35/ounce (now over $1,600). Samaszko lived modestly despite his wealth, withdrawing only $500 monthly. His sole heir, substitute teacher Arlene Magdanz, will receive proceeds after $800,000 in fees and taxes. Authorities believe Samaszko's mother, who died in 1992, acquired most coins.

article_content: Police required three weeks to evict 14 squatters from 101-year-old stroke survivor Megan Wilkinson's Peterborough home after she moved to a care facility. The family discovered the occupation through letting agents visiting the vacant property, which was intended for rental income to cover medical expenses. Authorities initially classified it as a civil matter, requiring a £4,000 court-ordered eviction. Following intervention by MP Stewart Jackson, police reassessed the case and peacefully removed the occupants. The property exhibited damage including scattered rubbish, bedding, and signs of smoking. Neighbors recalled Mrs. Wilkinson as a respected community member who moved to Germany four years prior. Cambridgeshire Police confirmed an ongoing review of their procedures.

Die Familie entdeckte die illegale Besetzung, als Makler das eigentlich zur Vermietung stehende Haus besichtigten – die Mieteinnahmen sollten Medikosten decken. Behörden stuften den Fall zunächst als zivilrechtlich ein, was einen 4.000-Pfund-Räumungsbeschluss erforderte. Nach Einschaltung des Abgeordneten Stewart Jackson ordnete die Polizei die Räumung an, die friedlich verlief. Das Haus wies Rauchspuren, verstreute Bettwaren und Müllberge auf. Nachbarn erinnerten sich an Frau Wilkinson als beliebte Anwohnerin, die vor vier Jahren nach Deutschland zog. Die Cambridgeshire Police überprüft nun ihr Vorgehen.

article_content: The March 16, 2014 referendum on Crimea's potential reunification with Russia became pivotal in the Ukraine crisis. Organized by Crimea's regional parliament, the vote's legality remains internationally disputed. Key points: 1. Referendum Context: Crimean voters (population ~2 million) chose between Ukrainian sovereignty or Russian integration. This followed Ukraine's political crisis involving mass protests, President Yanukovych's February 2014 removal, and subsequent Russian military deployment in Crimea. 2. Legal Perspectives: Ukraine's interim government and Western allies declared the vote unconstitutional. Russia contended the Kiev administration lost legitimacy after Yanukovych's ousting, which President Putin termed an 'anti-constitutional coup.' The U.S. emphasized Ukraine's constitutional requirement for nationwide referendums on territorial changes. 3. Historical & Strategic Factors: Transferred from Russia to Ukraine in 1954, Crimea hosts Russia's Black Sea Fleet in Sevastopol. Western sanctions threats contrast with EU-Russia economic interdependencies, particularly with Germany. 4. International Ramifications: While Russia drew parallels to Kosovo's independence precedent, U.S. officials discouraged historical comparisons. Analysts noted potential long-term impacts on Russia-Ukraine relations and security concerns among former Soviet states.

Die vom Regionalparlament der Krim organisierte Abstimmung bleibt international umstritten. Kernpunkte: 1. Hintergrund: Die etwa 2 Millionen Krim-Bewohner stimmten über den Verbleib in der Ukraine oder den Anschluss an Russland ab. Dies folgte auf die ukrainische politische Krise mit Massenprotesten, der Amtsenthebung von Präsident Janukowytsch im Februar 2014 und dem anschließenden Stationieren russischer Truppen auf der Halbinsel. 2. Rechtliche Standpunkte: Die ukrainische Übergangsregierung und westliche Staaten erklärten das Referendum für verfassungswidrig. Russland bestritt die Legitimität der Kiewer Regierung nach Janukowytschs Entmachtung, die Putin als 'verfassungsfeindlichen Putsch' bezeichnete. Die USA verwiesen auf die ukrainische Verfassung, die für Gebietsänderungen landesweite Volksabstimmungen vorschreibt. 3. Historische und strategische Aspekte: Die 1954 von der Russischen SFSR an die Ukrainische SSR übertragene Krim beheimatet die russische Schwarzmeerflotte in Sewastopol. Westliche Sanktionsandrohungen stehen im Spannungsverhältnis zu den eng verflochtenen Wirtschaftsbeziehungen zwischen EU-Ländern wie Deutschland und Russland. 4. Internationale Folgen: Während Russland Parallelen zum Kosovo-Präzedenzfall zog, warnten US-Vertreter vor historischen Gleichsetzungen. Experten betonten mögliche Langzeitauswirkungen auf die russisch-ukrainischen Beziehungen und Besorgnisse anderer postsowjetischer Staaten.

Sanderson's Floating Lotus studio in Helensvale and partnership with equipment provider JM SUP enable expanded coastal classes from Currumbin to Surfers Point. The reception crowd erupted in cheers, initially mistaking his performance for technical mishaps before recognizing the personal tribute.

article_content: Wolves reignited their promotion challenge with a 2-0 win against Middlesbrough, halting the visitors' seven-match Championship unbeaten run. Bakary Sako's cleverly chipped penalty (33') and Nouha Dicko's individual brilliance (73') secured the victory at Molineux. The triumph came at a cost as both goalscorers sustained injuries. Sako left with a groin problem while Dicko suffered a muscular issue, though manager Kenny Jackett stated both have 'reasonable recovery timelines.' Middlesbrough's Aitor Karanka lamented defensive errors: 'We knew Sako and Dicko were dangerous but failed to contain them.' Boro dominated second-half chances, with Patrick Bamford and Jelle Vossen hitting the crossbar and forcing goalkeeper Carl Ikeme into crucial saves. A contentious moment occurred when Wolves defender Ethan Ebanks-Landell blocked a shot with his arm, but referee Carl Berry dismissed Boro's appeals. Wolves nearly added to their lead earlier through Lee Evans and Dave Edwards, who both struck the woodwork from promising positions. The victory lifts Wolves to fourth place, though potential January absences for Sako and Dicko due to Africa Cup of Nations duty remain a concern. The duo have jointly contributed 11 goals this season, establishing themselves as one of the league's most formidable attacking pairs.

article_content: In der Region des Urdd Eisteddfod in Caerphilly finden sich Ortsnamen mit außergewöhnlichen Ursprüngen. Die Rhymni-Flussnamen entwickelten sich von 'Remni' (1101) zu 'Rhymni' – möglicherweise abgeleitet vom altwalisischen 'rhwmp' (Meißel), was den erosiven Flussverlauf beschreibt. Crumlins Name stammt vom walisischen 'Crymlyn' (gewundener See), anglisiert durch kartografische Fehler. Der Ort Nelson erhielt seinen Namen von einer 1803 erbauten Taverne, die zwei Jahre vor Lord Nelsons Tod in Trafalgar (1805) entstand. Die Bezeichnung 'Fleur-de-lis' geht auf französische Hugenottenflüchtlinge des 17. Jahrhunderts zurück, während Senghenydd durch das Grubenunglück von 1913 traurige Berühmtheit erlangte. Historische Karten dokumentieren die evolutionäre Schreibweise von Caerphilly selbst – von 'Caerfilly' bis zur heutigen Form.
translated_content: In the Caerphilly Urdd Eisteddfod region, place names boast fascinating etymologies. The River Rhymni's name transitioned from 'Remni' (1101) to its current spelling, potentially rooted in the Old Welsh 'rhwmp' (chisel), reflecting its erosive course. Crumlin derives from the Welsh 'Crymlyn' meaning 'crooked lake', later anglicized by mapmakers. Nelson village took its name from a tavern established in 1803 honoring Lord Nelson, predating his famous 1805 Trafalgar demise. The 'Fleur-de-lis' designation originates from 17th-century French Huguenot settlers, while Senghenydd became tragically renowned for the 1913 colliery disaster that claimed 439 lives. Caerphilly itself appears on historical maps as 'Caerfilly', showcasing gradual orthographic standardization.

article_content: Strolling through northern New Mexico's lush meadows and crystal-clear streams, national parks enthusiast Mikah Meyer found it hard to believe this serene landscape was once a volcanic battleground. Just 12,000 years ago, a supervolcano erupted violently, carving out the massive 21-kilometer Valles Caldera - twice the size of similar geological formations. The preserve's picturesque grasslands and azure waters mask its explosive past as the site of North America's largest volcanic event. 'This grassy bowl surrounded by mountains is unreal,' Mikah remarked. 'Coming from New Mexico's dry peaks, seeing 500 elk grazing here yesterday blew my mind! The prairie dog colonies alone span acres.' Now protected by the National Park Service, Valles Caldera boasts the Southwest's largest elk herds alongside diverse wildlife from Gunnison's prairie dogs to golden eagles. The road to Chaco Culture National Historical Park proved nightmarish. Mikah wandered lost for hours in desert backroads before finding the remote site. '30 miles of brutal gravel roads!' he recalled. 'I crawled at 2mph, van shaking violently. Nearly stranded without gas!' His ordeal paid off at Chaco Canyon, where 40,000 archaeological sites and 25 monumental 'great houses' reveal 15,000 years of human history. Freshly minted as a 2023 International Dark Sky Park, Chaco's stellar night views come with frequent UFO sighting reports from visitors. In stark contrast, Mikah dismissed Aztec Ruins as 'skippable' - just crumbling walls and a cramped 100-room structure some researchers controversially claim was an ancient prison. 'New Mexico's 'Land of Enchantment' nickname holds true,' he concluded. 'From Carlsbad's caves to White Sands' dunes... though maybe skip the underwhelming Aztec Ruins.'
